es: Reseñar una escena con presente narrativo, dos oraciones enfáticas y una valoración razonada.

teaching.en: In the climax, the teacher opens the door, sees the empty room and freezes, and the whole audience seems to hold its breath.
teaching.es: En el clímax, la profesora abre la puerta, ve la sala vacía y se queda inmóvil, y todo el público parece contener la respiración.
teaching.explanationEs: Climax = momento de máxima intensidad; freeze = quedarse inmóvil. Todo en presente narrativo.
segments: In the climax, the teacher opens the door, sees the empty room
and freezes, and the whole audience seems to hold its breath.
teaching.audioText: In the climax, the teacher opens the door, sees the empty room and freezes, and the whole audience seems to hold its breath.

teaching.en: The moment she reveals the secret, the silence in the room becomes so heavy that nobody dares to move.
teaching.es: En el momento en que revela el secreto, el silencio en la sala se vuelve tan pesado que nadie se atreve a moverse.
teaching.explanationEs: Reveal = revelar; silence = silencio; the moment + presente = en cuanto ocurre algo.
segments: The moment she reveals the secret, the silence in the
room becomes so heavy that nobody dares to move.
teaching.audioText: The moment she reveals the secret, the silence in the room becomes so heavy that nobody dares to move.

teaching.en: As the scene begins to unfold, what makes it gripping is not the dialogue but the silence between the two characters.
teaching.es: A medida que la escena empieza a desarrollarse, lo que la hace absorbente no es el diálogo sino el silencio entre los dos personajes.
teaching.explanationEs: Unfold = desarrollarse poco a poco; What makes … is … es la oración enfática.
segments: As the scene begins to unfold, what makes it gripping is
not the dialogue but the silence between the two characters.
teaching.audioText: As the scene begins to unfold, what makes it gripping is not the dialogue but the silence between the two characters.

teaching.en: The director uses a small detail, such as an empty chair, to convey sadness without a single word of explanation.
teaching.es: El director usa un pequeño detalle, como una silla vacía, para transmitir tristeza sin una sola palabra de explicación.
teaching.explanationEs: Detail = detalle; convey = transmitir una emoción o idea.
segments: The director uses a small detail, such as an empty
chair, to convey sadness without a single word of explanation.
teaching.audioText: The director uses a small detail, such as an empty chair, to convey sadness without a single word of explanation.

teaching.en: A long silence builds tension, and the slow pace will pay off if the ending can suggest that nothing will ever be the same again.
teaching.es: Un silencio largo genera tensión, y el ritmo lento dará resultado si el final puede sugerir que nada volverá a ser igual.
teaching.explanationEs: Tension = tensión; pay off = dar resultado; suggest = sugerir sin decirlo.
segments: A long silence builds tension, and the slow pace will pay off if
the ending can suggest that nothing will ever be the same again.
teaching.audioText: A long silence builds tension, and the slow pace will pay off if the ending can suggest that nothing will ever be the same again.

teaching.en: Overall, this is the turning point of the story, because in one short moment the audience learns the truth and the main character loses control.
teaching.es: En conjunto, este es el punto de inflexión de la historia, porque en un breve momento el público descubre la verdad y el protagonista pierde el control.
teaching.explanationEs: Turning point = punto de inflexión; Overall abre la valoración final.
segments: Overall, this is the turning point of the story, because in one short
moment the audience learns the truth and the main character loses control.
teaching.audioText: Overall, this is the turning point of the story, because in one short moment the audience learns the truth and the main character loses control.

feedback.es: Las tres acciones van en presente (opens, reads, starts); las otras versiones mezclan pasado y presente.

hint.es: Todos los verbos de la secuencia deben ir en presente.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que hace absorbente la escena es el silencio, no el diálogo.»

feedback.es: It is + lo destacado + that + verbo destaca un elemento: It is the small detail that conveys…

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una reseña con su función.

pairs: It works because the audience fears the truth.

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige qué sugiere la ventana abierta.

choices.text: That the officer has forgotten to close the window.
That somebody left the house only moments before.
That the kitchen is too cold for anybody to stay.

feedback.es: La ventana abierta es el detalle que sugiere que alguien acaba de irse, sin que nadie lo diga.

origin.audio: In my favourite scene the officer walks into the kitchen, opens the fridge and freezes. Nobody says a word. What makes the moment gripping is not what she finds, but the silence that follows, and it is the small detail of the open window that suggests somebody has just left. The scene works because the audience understands the whole story before the officer does.

prompt.es: Escribe una oración enfática: «Lo que más me conmovió fue el silencio.»

answer.text: What moved me most was the silence.
accepted: What moved me most was the silence.
What I found most moving was the silence.
What moved me most was the silence of the scene.

feedback.es: What moved me most was… destaca el silencio con la oración enfática.

origin.text: Lo que más me conmovió fue el silencio.

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige qué revela la decisión de la protagonista.

choices.text: The long speech she gives on the pier.
The music that begins when she leaves.
The tickets moving away on the water.

feedback.es: Son los billetes que se alejan sobre el agua los que revelan su decisión; no hay música ni discurso.

origin.audio: The scene at the harbour is the turning point of the film. The woman stands on the pier, takes out the two tickets and throws them into the sea. There is no music and no speech, just the sound of the waves. What makes the moment strong is the silence, and it is the tickets moving away on the water that reveal her decision. Some viewers find it too slow, but I think the slow pace is exactly why it pays off.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué postura defiende el crítico sobre el ritmo lento.

choices.text: That it is justified because it makes the scene stronger.
That it is the main problem of the scene.
That it should be cut from the final version.

feedback.es: Admite que algunos espectadores lo ven lento, pero sostiene que por eso la escena da resultado: defiende el ritmo.

feedback.es: Unfold describe algo que se desarrolla poco a poco, como una escena cuya tensión crece.

origin.text: At first nothing seems to happen. As the scene begins to ___, the audience slowly realises that the door will never open.

prompt.es: Escribe tu reseña de la escena: narra, destaca y valora.

answer.text: In the climax of the film, a teacher opens the door of her empty classroom on the night of the parents' meeting. She sees a chair, a letter on her desk and nothing else. She reads the letter slowly, drops her keys and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she switches off the light and leaves. What makes this moment so gripping is the silence: nobody speaks, but we understand everything. It is the small detail of the empty chair that conveys her sadness, because it shows that nobody came. The performance is understated, and the slow pace will pay off, since the tension keeps growing. Overall, I think it is the turning point of the film, because the audience learns the truth without a single line of dialogue.
accepted: In the climax of the film, a teacher opens the door of her empty classroom on the night of the parents' meeting. She sees a chair, a letter on her desk and nothing else. She reads the letter slowly, drops her keys and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she switches off the light and leaves. What makes this moment so gripping is the silence: nobody speaks, but we understand everything. It is the small detail of the empty chair that conveys her sadness, because it shows that nobody came. The performance is understated, and the slow pace will pay off, since the tension keeps growing. Overall, I think it is the turning point of the film, because the audience learns the truth without a single line of dialogue.

In the final scene, a teacher walks into her empty classroom after the parents' meeting and stops at the door. A letter lies on her desk next to an empty chair. She opens the letter, reads it slowly and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she puts out the light and walks away. What stays in the mind is the silence, because nobody explains what has happened. It is the empty chair that suggests her sadness, and it is the pause that builds the tension. The acting is understated, and the scene is moving because it trusts the audience. Overall, it works as the turning point of the film, since the truth is learned without one word of dialogue.

feedback.es: Una buena reseña narra en presente, destaca lo más importante con what o it is … that y justifica su valoración con because.

origin.text: Escena: una profesora abre la puerta de su aula vacía la noche de la reunión de padres. En su mesa hay una silla vacía y una carta. Ella la lee despacio, deja caer las llaves y no dice nada durante diez segundos. Después apaga la luz y se va. Escribe tu reseña: narra la escena en presente, usa dos oraciones enfáticas y da una valoración razonada.

prompt.es: Lee la reseña. ¿Con qué propósito evita el director mostrar el accidente?

choices.text: To save money by avoiding an expensive scene.
To let the audience imagine the event through the mother's reaction.
To keep the viewers guessing until the very end about what really happened.

feedback.es: La cámara se queda en el rostro de la madre: el director deja que el público imagine el accidente a partir de su reacción.

origin.text: Review extract: 'The director never shows the accident. Instead, the camera stays on the mother's face as she opens the door, and the silence tells us everything we need to know.'

prompt.es: Completa: «El final es tan hábil que por fin la lenta primera hora da resultado.»

feedback.es: Pay off significa dar resultado; aquí, la lentitud inicial se justifica gracias al final.

origin.text: The first hour is slow, and some viewers walk out. The ending is so good that the slow opening finally pays ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esa escena es el punto de inflexión porque el público descubre la verdad.»

answer.text: That scene is the turning point because the audience learns the truth

feedback.es: Because introduce la razón: el público descubre la verdad, y eso convierte la escena en el punto de inflexión.
